items.stem: Give evidences to show that the science of heredity is not new.
items.answer: The following evidences show that the science of heredity is not new: (i) Selective breeding of horses and cattle used to be done by the ancient civilisations of Babylon and Assyria. (ii) Ancient Chinese writings mention about creating better varieties of paddy. (iii) Ancient Indian medical practitioners were aware of the factors that determine the sex of a child.

items.stem: If the sperm, bearing Y-chromosome, fertilizes the egg, the child born will not be entirely like his father. Why is it so?
items.answer: It is so because the other sex chromosome which comes from the mother (i.e., X) as well as the 22 autosomes of the egg will also have their effects.

items.stem: Why are the chances of variation more in sexually developing organisms?
items.answer: The chances of variation are more in sexually developing organisms because meiosis (crossing over) occurs in gametogenesis and there is also fusion of gametes from two different individuals.
items.ocr: Solution printed 'game to genesis'; repaired to 'gametogenesis'.

items.stem: What are the rules of inheritance?
items.answer: On the basis of his experiments, Mendel established some rules which are called the rules of inheritance. They are (i) Law of Dominance, (ii) Law of Segregation and (iii) Law of Independent Assortment.
items.ocr: The printed question number was dropped by OCR (the text runs straight from question 71's answer into 'What are the rules of inheritance ?'); inferred as 72 from its position between 71 and 73.

items.stem: What is a sex chromosome?
items.answer: A sex chromosome is one which helps in sex determination of an organism. In human males, the sex chromosomes are XY and the gametes (sperms) they produce are of two types: X-bearing and Y-bearing. In females, the sex chromosomes are XX and the gametes (eggs) they produce are of only one type: X-bearing.
items.ocr: Solution printed 'sexdetermination' as one word; split.

items.stem: How do the traits get expressed?
items.answer: DNA is the source of genetic information for making proteins in the cell. The section of functional DNA is called a gene. For example, the height of a plant depends on a hormone. The amount of the hormone depends on the process of its formation. A protein is important for this process. If this protein works efficiently, a lot of hormone will be made. If the gene responsible for that protein has an alteration that makes the protein less efficient, the amount of hormone will be less and the plant will be short. Thus, genes control genetic characteristics or traits of an organism.
items.ocr: Solution printed 'The section of function DNA'; read as 'functional DNA'.

items.stem: How can we say that a change in genes can bring about a change in DNA?
items.answer: Genes are the functional part of DNA, thus genes are made up of DNA. If any gene gets changed, then it will also change the DNA structure of the organism.
items.ocr: Printed stem read 'How can we say that change in genes can be brought about the change in DNA?'; the broken grammar was straightened. Solution read 'If any get changed' — restored to 'If any gene gets changed'.

items.stem: Is it correct to say that if fertilization of the egg occurs on a full moon night, the child produced will be a male? Give reason.
items.answer: No, sex of the child is a matter of chance. Full moon has nothing to do with the sex of the child. The sperm having either X-chromosome or Y-chromosome, which fertilizes the egg, will determine the sex.

items.stem: What is the effect of high temperature on the sex-determination in turtle (Chrysema picta) and the lizard (Agama agama)?
items.answer:
(i) In turtle (Chrysema picta), high temperature during incubation results in the development of female progeny.
(ii) In the case of lizard (Agama agama), high incubation temperature results in male progeny.

items.stem: Why is variation beneficial for the species, but not necessary for the individual?
items.answer: Variation in a species enables it to adapt according to the changes and the new needs. This provides a survival advantage to the species. But an individual does not get any advantage due to a variation that takes place in him. Thus, variation is beneficial for a species, but not necessarily for the individual.

items.stem: With the help of X and Y show the sex determination in human beings.
items.answer: The printed answer is a diagram of the human sex-determination cross: mother (XX) × father (XY). All eggs of the mother carry an X chromosome, while the father's sperms are of two types, X-bearing and Y-bearing. X (egg) + X (sperm) → XX zygote, a girl; X (egg) + Y (sperm) → XY zygote, a boy.

items.stem:
The genotype of green stemmed tomato plants is denoted as GG and that of purple stemmed tomato plants as gg. When these two are crossed:
(i) What colour of stem would you expect in their F₁ progeny?
(ii) What is the percentage of purple stemmed in F₂ progeny if F₁ plants are self-pollinated?
(iii) In what ratio would you find the genotype of GG and Gg in the F₂ progeny?
items.answer:
(i) F₁ progeny – All Green.
(ii) Purple stemmed plants – 25%.
(iii) Ratio of GG and Gg is 1 : 2.
Purple stem × Green stem → Phenotype: Green stem : Purple stem = 3 : 1; Genotype: GG : Gg : gg = 1 : 2 : 1.

items.stem: "The sex of the children is determined by what they inherit from their father and not their mother". Justify.
items.answer: It is because a child who inherits an X chromosome from the sperm of the father will be a girl, and one who inherits a Y chromosome from the sperm of the father will be a boy. But all children will inherit an X chromosome from their mother regardless of whether they are boys or girls.

items.stem: Mention five characteristics of a gene.
items.answer:
(i) Gene is a unit of inheritance.
(ii) It is a segment of functional DNA on a chromosome occupying a specific position.
(iii) It is a unit of genetic information which codes for a specific trait or protein synthesis.
(iv) It can maintain uniformity through generations.
(v) It can undergo sudden heritable changes known as mutations.

items.stem:
In humans, genetically the sex of a child is determined by the father and not by the mother. Explain.
Or
Describe how the sex of the offspring is determined in the zygote in human beings.
Or
What is the basis of sex determination at the time of fertilization in humans?
Or
Explain the mechanism of sex-determination in the zygote.
items.answer: In humans, genetically the sex of a child is determined by the father and not by the mother because in the father there are two types of sex chromosomes present, X and Y, whereas in the mother both sex chromosomes are X. Hence, a male child will be born if a sperm carrying the Y-chromosome fertilizes the egg, while a female child will be born if a sperm carrying the X-chromosome fertilizes the egg.
